summary.text: One of the twenty-three suitors from Same on Cephallenia in Apollodorus' catalogue — a mortal namesake of Cerberus the hound of Hades, wholly distinct from the chthonic beast of Heracles' twelfth labour.

story.text: Apollodorus names Cerberus among the wooers assigned to Same, listed after Antisthenes and before Perimedes in Epitome 7.28 — a man who shares the hound's name and nothing more.
Homer knows the underworld hound without the name Cerberus; Hesiod, Apollodorus, and Hyginus make Cerberus the brazen-voiced guard of Hades whom Heracles fetched up — not this Cephallenian wooer.
